fg-faint.note: Disabled text and decorative icons only.

accent-focus.note: rgb(var(--accent) / var(--accent-focus-alpha)): the 2px ring on a focused field or the composer. Full strength in light, 50% in dark (accent-focus-dark), where it still clears 3:1 on the surface.

hl-key.note: Same in both themes. Reserved for the source being read.

hl-key-fg.note: Numerals on the lit key; same in both themes. Part of the litKey recipe.

hl-key-ring.note: Inset ring of the lit key, used at 50%; same in both themes. Part of the litKey recipe.

hl-soft.note: Lit card fill. Dark value hl-soft-dark #3D3120 (amber-500 at 14% over the surface): reads as amber, not khaki; Muted Ink 4.9:1, Link Teal 8.6:1, Ink 11.5:1.

hl-ring.note: Lit card border. Dark value hl-ring-dark #956516 (amber-500 at 55% over the surface).

sweep.note: Registered @property --sweep so the completion sweep can fade the colour.

mark.note: AppMark, favicon and brand files only: mark #099B94, mark-ink #102D46 (zinc-200 in dark), mark-hl #C4E64B. Wordmark is Ink.

narrative.overview:
This is the clinical-reference category standard played straight, at full craft, beside OpenEvidence, UpToDate, Perplexity and Notion. The page is a white canvas (zinc-900 at night) with a near-white zinc history rail, zinc text and hairlines, and one deep clinical teal. Nothing on the chrome competes with the answer: the question is the page title, the answer sits in a serif reading column of about 68 characters, and the evidence margin lists the cited sources as flat bordered cards beside it. Light and dark themes follow the system setting through semantic CSS variables, so no component branches on theme for surfaces, text or lines.

Colour is spent on meaning, not mood. Teal says "act here" (the primary button, links, focus, the caret). Amber says "this is the source you are reading": the highlighter sweep across a claim, the lit citation key and the lit card. Evidence levels use Tailwind UI ring-inset badges in categorical hues. Everything else is zinc.

Density is reference-tool density: compact semibold UI in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, generous serif leading for the answer, hairline dividers instead of boxes wherever a list will do. The world refuses the replaced printout look's coloured shell, heavy ink rules and candy tints, and refuses a centred chat column with sources dumped underneath.
keyCharacteristics: White / zinc-900 canvas, zinc hairlines, one clinical teal accent.
Amber reserved for the source being read.
STIX Two Text for answer prose and findings; Atkinson Hyperlegible Next at semibold for UI.
Answer column and evidence margin side by side from xl; source sheet below xl.
Flat bordered cards; soft small shadows only on controls; real lift only for menus and the sheet.
Themes follow the system; every surface, text and line colour is a semantic token.

rules.name: The Amber Means Reading Rule
rules.body: Amber marks the source being read now: the claim sweep, the lit citation key, the lit card's fill and ring, the sheet's position key. No evidence level uses amber (Observational is orange). The one other amber in the product is the image-identifier caution in the composer, a single amber-50 note with amber-900 text and a ShieldAlert icon; it is a sanctioned one-off, not a warning style. The AppMark's lime line depicts the same act of reading a cited claim, in the brand's own colour; lime never enters the interface.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Teal is the only accent. Primary action, links and text actions, focus, caret, selected mode and selection all draw from it; no second brand hue enters the chrome.

rules.name: The Neutral Disabled Rule
rules.body: A disabled primary button is a neutral fill (Ink at 7%) with a Faint Ink label and no shadow, in both themes. It never shows a faded accent.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: STIX Two Text is for what a source or the answer says; Atkinson Hyperlegible Next at semibold is for everything the interface says. Never set UI chrome in the serif or answer prose in the sans.

rules.name: The One Scale Rule
rules.body: Sizes come from the seven-step scale (0.75, 0.8125, 0.9375, 1.09375, 1.3125, 1.875, 2.625rem). Numbers in keys, counts and dates use lining tabular figures.

rules.name: The Counts Once Rule
rules.body: The "n cited · N reviewed" counts appear once per breakpoint: in the evidence margin header from xl up, and below xl in the meta strip as the teal underlined button that opens the source sheet. The date and answer time live only in the running header.

rules.name: The One Right Edge Rule
rules.body: The question rule, answer, related questions and composer share one right edge, the 37.5rem measure.

rules.name: The Soft Edge Rule
rules.body: A scroller that ends at a docked band or a sticky edge fades its content out over 1.5rem with a mask-image (the .scroll-edges class and useScrollEdges hook), never a painted gradient overlay, so it fades to whatever lies behind in either theme. The fade appears only while more content lies past that edge, and grows in over 200ms. The thread fades at its bottom, above the composer dock; the evidence margin fades at both ends. The running header keeps its hard hairline: it is a header, not a scroll edge.

rules.name: The Flat Card Rule
rules.body: Source cards are flat: a hairline border, no shadow, in every state. Lighting a card changes its fill and border to amber; it never lifts. The hanging numbered key is the exception on the card: opaque Surface, a Firm Hairline ring and the control shadow, so it reads over the gutter.

dos: **Do** draw every surface, text and line colour from the semantic tokens, so light and dark follow the system without component branches.
**Do** keep teal for action, links, focus, caret and the selected mode, and keep amber for the source being read.
**Do** set answer prose and card findings in STIX Two Text at the 37.5rem measure; set all UI in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, semibold for labels and actions.
**Do** keep source cards flat with a hairline border, and light them by fill and border only.
**Do** show the cited and reviewed counts once per breakpoint: margin header from xl, meta-strip button below xl.
**Do** use hairline-divided rows for lists of choices and the evidence badge palette for evidence levels.
**Do** end a scroller at a docked band or sticky edge with the mask fade, shown only while there is more to scroll.
donts: **Don't** use amber for an evidence level, a status or a generic warning; the composer's image-identifier caution is the only amber note.
**Don't** fade the accent for a disabled primary button; use the neutral Ink-7% fill.
**Don't** add shadows to source cards, or raise anything above the control shadow except menus and the sheet.
**Don't** introduce a second accent hue or a coloured app shell.
**Don't** add a second Canada chip; the mark lives in the byline.
**Don't** repeat the date, answer time or counts in more than one place at a breakpoint.
**Don't** load favicons or logos from a third-party service; publisher marks are drawn locally.
**Don't** give publisher tiles a hue; the categorical hues belong to the evidence badges.
